title: Tenali Raman Tale 136 (മലയാളം)

full_text:
During an afternoon hunting expedition in the rocky crags of Anegundi, King Krishnadevaraya’s prized northern hunting hawk, Garud, slipped its jesses and flew into the dense mountain forest.
The King was heartbroken: the bird was loyal, had saved the King from a poisonous cobra years before, and responded only to a silver whistle.
Three companies of soldiers beat the bushes for two days, blowing horns and shouting, but the hawk was nowhere to be found.

The King fell into deep gloom, refusing to hold court.
Tenali Raman volunteered: 'Maharaj, hawks do not respond to beating drums and shouting soldiers; noise drives them higher into the peaks. Allow me to bring Garud back before sunset.'

Tenali did not take soldiers or drums.
He took a small wicker basket containing three fat, live field quail—a hawk’s favorite prey—and a small brass pan of fresh sheep’s liver seasoned with aromatic oil.
Tenali also took the King’s silver hunting whistle.

Tenali climbed to a high, rocky plateau overlooking the forested valley where the bird was lost.
He observed the afternoon sky:
High above the thermal updrafts, circling gracefully on mountain winds, was a solitary raptor with a distinctive white wing-band. It was Garud!

Tenali did not shout or wave.
He placed the fragrant liver on a flat, sun-warmed granite boulder where the rising thermals would carry its scent upward.
Then Tenali tied one live quail by its leg to a peg in the soft grass, allowing it to flutter its wings gently.
Tenali hid beneath a camouflaged screen of wild fern branches, held the silver whistle to his lips, and blew the King’s exact three-note hunting call:
*‘TWEET... TWEET-TWEEE!’*

High in the sky, the hawk heard the familiar silver whistle and caught the scent of warm meat!
Seeing the fluttering quail below, Garud folded its wings and executed a breathtaking, vertical dive from the clouds!
*WHOOOOSH!*

The hawk landed gracefully upon the granite boulder, digging its talons into the meat.
Tenali emerged slowly from the ferns, speaking gentle, soothing words in the falconer's dialect, and extended his leather-gloved arm:
The magnificent bird recognized the gentle voice, hopped calmly onto Tenali’s wrist, and allowed the leather jesses to be fastened!

Tenali carried the hawk back to the palace.
When King Krishnadevaraya saw his beloved hunting companion perched safely on Tenali’s wrist, tears of joy filled the Emperor's eyes!
The King rewarded Tenali with a diamond armlet, celebrating that understanding the nature of living creatures accomplishes what an army cannot.
moral: Careful inquiry into natural habits recovers lost companions where blind searching fails. [ML]
